items.title: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tech
items.excerpt: The UK's independent immigration watchdog is considering a probe into the Home Office's use of ChatGPT-based tools to summarise and process asylum claims, amid concerns over accuracy and secrecy about how the tools are used.

items.title: Lords asks government to think again on Cyber Security Bill (AISI powers review agreed 202-155; frontier-AI incident-reporting amendment defeated)
items.excerpt: At report stage on 26 October the House of Lords defeated the government 202-155 to write into the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill a review that must consider giving the AI Security Institute powers; a separate amendment requiring frontier AI developers to report incidents was defeated 95-165, while a government amendment lets ministers take powers where an AI agent loses oversight or control of a regulated network.
items.note: vote details per Hansard 2026-10-26 and resultsense.com analysis (https://resultsense.com/insights/2026-10-27-aisi-voluntary-access-lords-review-cyber-bill/)

items.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
items.excerpt: A Delaware corporate-law proposal would allow AI agents to run entire companies with no human at the helm; US Rep. Comer warns owners of AI-run firms could evade liability for 'reckless' AI.

items.title: INEC Probes Suspected AI-Generated Photos In Voters' Register
items.excerpt: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission said in a statement it is investigating suspected AI-generated photographs found in the preliminary Register of Voters published online on October 26, reviewing records for technical or procedural lapses before the final register is certified on December 15, 2026.
items.off_list: channelstv.com - on-list sources had no coverage of this formal electoral-body action

items.title: 生成AIデータの透明性確保策 グーグルなど5社が日本政府に回答
items.excerpt: Japan's Cabinet Office on Oct 27 published the responses of Google and four other AI firms to the government's request for transparency about generative-AI training data, under the IP-protection principles that took effect Oct 26; Google said it does not store training data in its models.
items.off_list: asahi.com - primary is cao.go.jp (Cabinet Office) release; no on-list English coverage found

items.title: 정부, AI 청소년 보호 강화…심의·법제 정비 본격화
items.excerpt: Korea's Broadcasting, Media and Communications Commission is preparing a standalone 'AI Service User Protection Act' (provisional name) and moving to amend the Network Act and AI Basic Act as AI chatbots' harmful content and youth over-use draw scrutiny.
items.off_list: digitaltoday.co.kr - Korea policy coverage, no on-list item

items.title: [단독] 멜론 차트 2위가 AI 음악?…정부, 표시 의무 확대 검토
items.excerpt: After an AI-made track reached No. 2 on the Melon chart without disclosure, the Korean government is reviewing extending AI-generated content labeling obligations beyond AI providers to distribution platforms.
items.off_list: news1.kr - Korea policy; possible music cross-section overlap

items.title: 트럼프 "모든 분야서 AI용어 공식금지할 것"…또 SI 명칭 강요
items.excerpt: President Trump posted on Truth Social on Oct 27 that the US will 'officially ban' the term AI in all relevant official documents and fields, insisting on 'SI' (super intelligence), following last month's executive order requiring agencies to use SI in official documents.

items.title: UK Politician Jess Asato Got Deepfaked. Now She's Taking xAI to Court
items.excerpt: Labour MP Jess Asato, who campaigned for victims of online abuse, became a target of Grok-generated sexual deepfakes and is now pursuing legal action against xAI.
items.note: interview format; check for a new filing

items.title: UK ministers had plenty of time for AI datacenter bosses, but none for environmental groups
items.excerpt: An investigation of ministerial meeting records finds businesses dominated UK government meetings on AI Growth Zones while communities and environmental groups were left out.

items.title: Britain bets big on AI to defend against the threats AI is helping create
items.excerpt: Whitehall wants AI agents guarding critical national infrastructure as part of a wider GBP600M cyber spending plan.

items.title: The U.S.-Taiwan ART's Export Control Puzzle
items.excerpt: Analysis of what the export-control 'alignment' clause in the US-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade requires of Taipei for advanced chips and AI hardware.

items.title: The UK-US Tech Deal Exposes the Limits of Britain's AI Ambitions
items.excerpt: Megan Kirkwood argues completion of the UK-US Tech Prosperity Deal will be a crucial test of the new Labour government and exposes how dependent Britain's AI plans are on US firms.

items.title: Without an Exit Plan, AI Partnerships Risk Becoming the New Tied Aid
items.excerpt: Rachel George argues government AI partnerships risk binding recipient countries to donors' priorities, standards and suppliers, like tied aid.

items.title: Policy proposal would require firms to disclose how they use AI to develop new models
items.excerpt: A framework from Americans for Responsible Innovation would require AI developers to disclose how they use AI to build new models, as Jay Clayton's task force shapes the government's relationship with developers.

items.title: AI Hallucination Goes to Court: A Global Mapping of Emerging Legal Issues
items.excerpt: Wenlong Li maps court cases and legal responses worldwide on AI hallucinations, covering liability, accountability and defamation.

items.title: This AI Radio Host Speaks Spanish and Backs Immigrants. It's Winning Over Listeners
items.excerpt: Coyotec, a bilingual AI radio host that tells listeners how to defend themselves against ICE, is drawing a growing audience ahead of the midterms.

items.title: AI 윤리 '신호등' 세 개 섰다…정부 가이드라인 제정 "이제 시작"
items.excerpt: Korea's Education Ministry, National Research Foundation and Science ministry have each issued AI-ethics guidelines for universities within a year, but they are non-binding recommendations.

items.title: Police Are Using AI to Pull Over Drivers for 'Suspicious' Behavior
items.excerpt: The ACLU warns police are using AI-flagged license-plate travel patterns to stop drivers who have not broken any law.

items.title: Australia warns of 'unprecedented' AI threat
items.excerpt: The Australian Signals Directorate reported an 80% rise in warnings about potentially malicious activity over the past year and warned of an unprecedented AI-enabled threat.
